lessonActivities.title: What Is Reported Speech? 🗣️
lessonActivities.content:
When someone shares an idea and you want to tell another person about it later, you use reported (indirect) speech! Instead of quoting exact words, you report the meaning.

Direct Speech = exact words in quotation marks. Example: Tom said, 'I like football.'

Reported Speech = meaning without quotes. Example: Tom said (that) he liked football.

ElementDirect SpeechReported SpeechChange
Reporting Verbsaid / toldsaid / toldSame verb, different structure
PronounsI, you, myhe/she, I, his/herShift to match reporter's perspective
QuotesYesNoRemove quotation marks
'That'N/AOptionalCan be omitted after reporting verbs

Fun fact: The word 'that' is optional after reporting verbs—native speakers often drop it! ✨

Quick Rule: If the reporting verb is past (said/told), prepare to backshift. If present (says/tells), keep original tense.
examples: Direct: 'I want to go home.' → Reported: She said (that) she wanted to go home.
Direct: 'Can you help me?' → Reported: She asked if I could help her.
lessonActivities.tips: Quick Rule: If the reporting verb is past (said/told), prepare to backshift. If present (says/tells), keep original tense.

lessonActivities.title: Reporting Verbs: Say vs. Tell vs. Ask 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Now let's level up! 🎯 Not all reporting verbs work the same way. Say, tell, and ask have different patterns that you must master.

Formation: [Subject] + [reporting verb] + [object/person] + (that) + [clause]. Example: She told me (that) she was tired.

VerbPatternExampleKey Note
saysay + (that) + clauseHe said (that) he was busy.No person object needed
telltell + person + (that) + clauseShe told me (that) she was busy.Requires person object
askask + (person) + if/wh- + clauseHe asked if I was busy.For questions only
explainexplain + (to person) + (that) + clauseShe explained (to me) that it was late.'To' optional before person

Fun fact: You can't say 'She said me'—it must be 'She told me' or 'She said to me'! 🚫

Memory trick: SAY = no person needed. TELL = person required. ASK = for questions only.
examples: Correct: He said he was tired. / He told me he was tired.
Wrong: He said me he was tired. × → He told me he was tired. ✓
Question: 'Are you tired?' → He asked if I was tired.
functions: Choosing the correct reporting verb for context
lessonActivities.tips: Memory trick: SAY = no person needed. TELL = person required. ASK = for questions only.

lessonActivities.title: Pronoun Shifts in Reported Speech 👥
lessonActivities.content:
Time to explore another way! 👥 When reporting speech, pronouns must shift to match who is speaking and who is being addressed. This keeps your reported speech clear and logical.

Pattern: [Subject of reporting verb] + said/told + (that) + [pronoun-adjusted clause]. Example: Jane said, 'I need help' → Jane said she needed help.

Direct SpeechContextReported SpeechPronoun Change
'I am tired.'Tom speakingTom said he was tired.I → he
'You are late.'Teacher to studentThe teacher told me I was late.You → I
'We will win.'Team captainHe said they would win.We → they
'My car is broken.'Friend speakingShe said her car was broken.My → her

Fun fact: Possessive adjectives (my/your/our) change just like pronouns! 🔄

Decision point: Who said it? → Use their pronoun (he/she/they). Who were they talking to? → Adjust 'you' accordingly.
examples: With first person: 'I love music' → He said he loved music.
With second person: 'You should rest' → She told me I should rest.
In questions: 'Are you coming?' → He asked if I was coming.
functions: Handling possessive adjectives in reported speech
lessonActivities.tips: Decision point: Who said it? → Use their pronoun (he/she/they). Who were they talking to? → Adjust 'you' accordingly.

lessonActivities.title: Basic Tense Backshift: Present → Past ⏪
lessonActivities.content:
Here's where it gets interesting! ⏪ When the reporting verb is in the past, most present tenses shift 'back' to past. This is called tense backshift.

The Rule: After past reporting verbs (said/told), present tenses usually become past tenses. Example: 'I like coffee' → She said she liked coffee.

Direct TenseReported TenseExampleSignal
Present Simple→ Past Simple'I work here' → He said he worked hereGeneral facts, habits
Present Continuous→ Past Continuous'I'm working' → She said she was workingActions in progress
Present Perfect→ Past Perfect'I have finished' → He said he had finishedCompleted with relevance
Will→ Would'I'll call' → She said she would callFuture intentions

Fun fact: Past Perfect doesn't change—it's already as 'past' as it gets! 🎉

Common mistake: 'She said she is coming' × → 'She said she was coming' ✓

Pro tip: Look for the reporting verb first. If it's past (said/told), backshift the tense in the reported clause.
examples: Positive: 'I have finished' → She said she had finished.
Negative: 'I don't know' → He said he didn't know.
Question form: 'Do you understand?' → She asked if I understood.
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: Look for the reporting verb first. If it's past (said/told), backshift the tense in the reported clause.

lessonActivities.title: Removing Quotation Marks & Punctuation 📝
lessonActivities.content:
Ready for the next level? 📝 One of the simplest but most important changes in reported speech is removing quotation marks and adjusting punctuation.

Formation: Remove quotes, change capitalization, adjust punctuation. Example: 'I am tired.' → He said he was tired.

ElementDirect SpeechReported SpeechChange
Quotation MarksYes: "I'm busy."No: He said he was busy.Remove all quotes
CapitalizationStarts with capitalContinues sentenceLowercase after 'that'
Question MarkYes: "Are you OK?"No: He asked if I was OK.Use period, not question mark
ExclamationYes: "Great!"No: She said it was great.Use period, adjust verb

Fun fact: Reported questions never use question marks—they become statements! ❓→.

Common mistake: She said, "that she was tired" × → She said that she was tired. ✓

When to use: Always remove quotes in reported speech. Keep punctuation simple: usually just a period at the end.
examples: Statement: 'I like pizza.' → He said he liked pizza.
Question: 'Do you like pizza?' → She asked if I liked pizza.
Exclamation: 'What a great day!' → He exclaimed that it was a great day.
functions: Converting direct punctuation to reported form
lessonActivities.tips: When to use: Always remove quotes in reported speech. Keep punctuation simple: usually just a period at the end.

lessonActivities.title: Negative Statements in Reported Speech ❌
lessonActivities.content:
Let's master the full picture! ❌ Knowing how to report negative statements completes your control of basic reported speech.

Negative Formation: [Subject] + said/told + (that) + [subject] + didn't/wasn't/hadn't + [rest]. Example: 'I don't like coffee' → He said he didn't like coffee.

Direct NegativeStructure PatternReported FormKey Change
Present Simple Negdon't/doesn't + verbdidn't + verbdo/does → did
Present Continuous Negam/is/are + not + -ingwas/were + not + -ingam/is/are → was/were
Present Perfect Neghaven't/hasn't + past participlehadn't + past participlehave/has → had
Will Negwon't + verbwouldn't + verbwill → would

Fun fact: 'Don't' becomes 'didn't' in reported speech, not 'don't'—the auxiliary shifts too! 🔄

Common mistake: 'She said she don't like it' × → 'She said she didn't like it' ✓

Remember: In negatives, the auxiliary verb (do/does/is/have/will) backshifts just like the main verb.
examples: Negative statement: 'I don't know.' → He said he didn't know.
Negative continuous: 'I'm not working.' → She said she wasn't working.
Negative perfect: 'I haven't seen it.' → He said he hadn't seen it.
lessonActivities.tips: Remember: In negatives, the auxiliary verb (do/does/is/have/will) backshifts just like the main verb.

lessonActivities.title: When NOT to Backshift: General Truths ✨
lessonActivities.content:
Here's a crucial rule! ✨ Sometimes we don't backshift tenses in reported speech. This happens with general truths, scientific facts, and permanent situations.

The Exception: If the statement is always true or still true now, you can keep the present tense. Example: 'The Earth orbits the Sun' → She said the Earth orbits the Sun.

ContextBackshift?ExampleWhy?
General TruthOptional'Water boils at 100°C' → He said water boils/boiled at 100°C.Fact is always true
Still True NowOptional'I am 25' (said yesterday) → She said she is/was 25.Age hasn't changed
Reporting Verb PresentNo'I'm tired' → He says he is tired.Same time frame
Specific Past EventYes'I was tired yesterday' → He said he had been tired.Completed past action

Fun fact: In formal/academic writing, backshifting is often preferred even for general truths! 📚

Common mistake: Over-applying the exception. When in doubt, backshift—it's never wrong!

Master level: In casual speech, keep present tense for timeless facts. In formal writing, backshift for consistency.
examples: Scientific fact: 'The sun rises in the east.' → He said the sun rises/rose in the east.
Permanent situation: 'Paris is in France.' → She said Paris is/was in France.
Still true: 'I live in London.' → He said he lives/lived in London.
functions: Adapting reported speech to context and register
lessonActivities.tips: Master level: In casual speech, keep present tense for timeless facts. In formal writing, backshift for consistency.

lessonActivities.title: Mastery: Putting It All Together 🏆
lessonActivities.content:
You've come so far! 🏆 Let's tackle the complete transformation from direct to reported speech, combining all the rules you've learned.

Complete Checklist: 1) Choose reporting verb 2) Adjust pronouns 3) Backshift tenses (if needed) 4) Change time/place words 5) Remove quotes 6) Adjust punctuation.

StepActionExample Transformation
1. Reporting VerbSelect said/told/askedTom said...
2. PronounsI→he, you→I/me, my→his/her...'I like my car' → ...he liked his car
3. Tense BackshiftPresent→Past, will→would, etc....'like' → liked
4. Time/Placetoday→that day, here→there...'today' → that day
5. Remove QuotesDelete quotation marksRemove " " around the clause
6. PunctuationUse period, not question markEnd with . not ?

Fun fact: Native speakers often skip 'that' in casual speech—'He said he was tired' sounds more natural than 'He said that he was tired'! 💬

Mastery checklist: ✓ Reporting verb chosen ✓ Pronouns shifted ✓ Tenses backshifted (if needed) ✓ Time/place adjusted ✓ Quotes removed ✓ Punctuation fixed

Pro tip: Practice the full transformation step-by-step at first. With time, it becomes automatic!
examples: Full example: 'I will call you tomorrow.' → He said he would call me the next day.
Complex: 'I can't come today because I'm busy.' → She said she couldn't come that day because she was busy.
Question: 'Where did you go yesterday?' → He asked where I had gone the day before.
functions: Combining all reported speech rules in complex transformations
lessonActivities.tips: Pro tip: Practice the full transformation step-by-step at first. With time, it becomes automatic!

writingActivities.question: Report what your friend said about their weekend using basic reported speech. Include: a statement with said/told, a pronoun change, and remove quotation marks.
writingActivities.hint: Start with 'My friend said (that)...'. Change I→he/she, my→his/her. Example: My friend said that she was tired after work.

writingActivities.question: Convert this direct statement to reported speech: 'I like playing football on Saturdays.'
writingActivities.hint: Use said/told + backshift present simple to past simple. Example: He said he liked playing football on Saturdays.

writingActivities.question: Tell a short story about what your teacher announced in class today. Use reported speech at least twice.
writingActivities.hint: Begin with 'The teacher announced that...'. Add details with time markers like that day or the next day.
sentenceStarters: First, she announced... Then, she explained...

writingActivities.question: Describe a conversation where someone gave you advice. Use reported speech for the advice and include a modal verb (should/could/might).
writingActivities.hint: Remember: advised/suggested for advice. Modal verbs like 'should' often don't change in reported speech. Example: She advised me to study more, saying I should focus on grammar.

writingActivities.question: Compare what two different people said about the same event using reported speech. Show how their perspectives differed.
writingActivities.hint: Use however/although to show contrast between their statements. Add similarly/both if they agreed on something.
sentenceStarters: Both John and Mary said that..., but John added...

writingActivities.question: Write a paragraph reporting a news announcement. Use cause-effect markers to explain why the announcement was made.
writingActivities.hint: Start with the cause: because/since/as. Then show the result: therefore/so/consequently.

writingActivities.question: Express an opinion about a rule at school/work. Report what someone else said about it, then give your view.
writingActivities.hint: State your view with I believe/In my opinion. Support it with for example/this is because. Report others with said/told.
sentenceStarters: In my opinion,... because my teacher said that...
I believe that... as my colleague explained...

writingActivities.question: Describe a hypothetical situation using reported conditional speech. Include what someone said they would do if a condition were met.
writingActivities.hint: Use If + past simple, would + base verb in reported form. Example: She said that if it rained, she would stay home.
sentenceStarters: If I had enough time, I would... he said.
She mentioned that if..., she would...

writingActivities.question: Report a complex conversation involving a statement, a negative, and a general truth. Show mastery by using correct structures for each.
writingActivities.hint: This requires 3 different approaches: backshift for past statements, keep present for general truths, handle negatives correctly. Pay attention to pronoun shifts.
sentenceStarters: Although she said..., he explained that...
When I asked..., she replied that...

writingActivities.question: Write a formal email summarizing a meeting. Use reported speech to convey what colleagues said, with hedging language and polite conclusions.
writingActivities.hint: Maintain formal register: avoid contractions, use passive voice/formal connectors, end with polite closing. Report speech with stated/indicated/suggested.
sentenceStarters: One colleague suggested that, given the circumstances...

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct reported speech form:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I like ice cream.' → Reported: She said ____.
options: that she will like ice cream
that she had liked ice cream
gameActivities.hint: Present Simple in direct speech → Past Simple in reported speech when the reporting verb is past.

gameActivities.question: Select the right pronoun for reported speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Tom said: '____ am tired.' → Tom said that ____ was tired.
gameActivities.hint: First person 'I' in direct speech becomes third person (he/she) when reporting what someone else said.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct reporting verb:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'm busy.' → She ____ me that she was busy.
gameActivities.hint: Use 'told' when there's a person object (me/him/her). Use 'said' without a person object.

gameActivities.question: Choose whether to keep or remove quotation marks:
gameActivities.sentence: Reported speech: He said ____ he was tired.
gameActivities.hint: Reported speech does not use quotation marks. Remove them when converting from direct speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct negative form in reported speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I don't like coffee.' → Reported: He said he ____ coffee.
gameActivities.hint: Present Simple negative 'don't' backshifts to Past Simple negative 'didn't' in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'say' vs 'tell'?
options: She said me she was tired.
She told me she was tired.
She said to me that she was tired.
correctAnswer: She told me she was tired.
gameActivities.hint: 'Tell' requires a person object (me/him/her). 'Say' does not, or uses 'to + person'.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct tense backshift:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I am working now.' → Reported: She said she ____ then.
gameActivities.hint: Present Continuous backshifts to Past Continuous in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Select the appropriate form for a general truth:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Water boils at 100°C.' → Reported: He said water ____ at 100°C.
gameActivities.hint: General truths/scientific facts can keep present tense in reported speech.

gameActivities.question: Pick the correct punctuation for reported speech:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'Are you coming?' → Reported: She asked if I was coming ____
gameActivities.hint: Reported questions use statement punctuation (period), not question marks.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct pronoun shift for possessive adjectives:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'My car is broken.' → Reported: She said ____ car was broken.
gameActivities.hint: Possessive adjectives shift like pronouns: my→his/her, your→my/our, our→their.

gameActivities.question: Select the correct form when the reporting verb is present:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I am tired.' → Reported (immediate): He says he ____ tired.
gameActivities.hint: If the reporting verb is present (says), don't backshift the tense.

gameActivities.question: Advanced: Choose the most precise reported form:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I have been waiting for an hour.' → Reported: She said she ____ for an hour.
gameActivities.hint: Present Perfect Continuous backshifts to Past Perfect Continuous.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct form for reported speech with 'will':
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I will help you.' → Reported: He said he ____ me.
gameActivities.hint: 'Will' changes to 'would' in reported speech when the reporting verb is past.

gameActivities.question: Select the appropriate form showing no backshift for immediacy:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I am leaving now.' (said 2 minutes ago) → Reported: She says she ____ now.
gameActivities.hint: If reporting immediately or the situation is still current, backshift may not be needed.

gameActivities.question: Choose the correct complete transformation:
gameActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I can't come tomorrow because I'm busy.' → Reported: ____
options: She said she couldn't come the next day because she was busy.
She said she can't come tomorrow because she's busy.
She said she couldn't come tomorrow because she was busy.
She said she can't come the next day because she's busy.
correctAnswer: She said she couldn't come the next day because she was busy.
gameActivities.hint: Check: pronouns, tense backshift, time expression, and negation all changed correctly.

quizActivities.question: What is the main difference between direct and reported speech?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I am happy.' → Reported: She said ____.
quizActivities.hint: Reported speech usually removes quotes and may change pronouns/tense.
quizActivities.explanation: Reported speech reports the meaning without quotation marks. Pronouns and tenses often shift to match the reporting context.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses reported speech for a statement?
quizActivities.sentence: Choose the correct option: Tom said, 'I am happy.'
options: Tom said that he was happy.
Tom said that he is happy.
Tom said that he had been happy.
Tom said that he will be happy.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: Tom said that he was happy.
quizActivities.hint: Check subject-verb agreement and tense consistency.
quizActivities.explanation: This question tests basic reported speech usage. The correct answer follows the backshift rule: Present Continuous 'am' → Past Continuous 'was'.

quizActivities.question: Identify the reporting verb in this sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: She told me that she would call later.
quizActivities.hint: Look for the verb that introduces what someone said.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Told' is the reporting verb—it introduces the reported clause 'that she would call later'. 'Would call' is the reported action, not the reporting verb.

quizActivities.question: What is the correct reported form for this everyday statement?
options: He said he needed a break.
He said he needs a break.
He said he had needed a break.
He said he would need a break.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: He said he needed a break.
quizActivities.hint: Consider the register: is this formal or informal?
quizActivities.explanation: In everyday contexts with past reporting verb, we backshift: 'need' → 'needed'. Option B keeps present tense (acceptable only if reporting verb is present or fact is timeless).

quizActivities.question: Which word best completes this reported statement?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I like coffee.' → Reported: She said ____ she liked coffee.
quizActivities.hint: Do the ideas agree, contrast, or show cause-effect?
quizActivities.explanation: 'That' introduces reported statements. 'If/whether' are for reported yes/no questions. 'What/when' are for reported wh-questions.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'say' vs 'tell'?
options: She said me she was tired.
She told me she was tired.
She said to me that she was tired.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: She told me she was tired.
quizActivities.hint: Pay attention to the structure for reporting statements.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Tell' requires a person object (me/him/her). 'Say' does not, or uses 'to + person'. Only options B and D are grammatically possible; B is more natural.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct tense sequence for this reported narrative:
quizActivities.sentence: When I arrived, she said she ____ already left.
quizActivities.hint: Which action happened first? Use past perfect for the earlier action.
quizActivities.explanation: Past perfect (had + past participle) shows an action completed before another past action. She left BEFORE I arrived, so 'had already left' is correct in reported speech.

quizActivities.question: Select the appropriate pronoun change for reported speech:
quizActivities.sentence: Jane said: 'My brother is visiting.' → Jane said ____ brother was visiting.
quizActivities.hint: Whose brother is it? Adjust possessive to match the speaker.
quizActivities.explanation: When Jane speaks, 'my brother' refers to her brother. In reported speech, we shift to third person: 'her brother'. 'His' would refer to a male's brother; 'my' keeps first person incorrectly.

quizActivities.question: Which time expression correctly completes this reported sentence?
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I'll see you tomorrow.' → Reported: He said he would see me ____.
quizActivities.hint: Which preposition pairs with 'look' to mean 'search for information'?
quizActivities.explanation: 'Tomorrow' in direct speech usually becomes 'the next day' or 'the following day' in reported speech. 'Tomorrow' can stay only if reporting on the same day; 'yesterday/today' are incorrect shifts.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct word order for this reported statement:
quizActivities.sentence: Direct: 'I don't understand.' → Reported: She said ____.
quizActivities.hint: Question word + subject + backshifted verb (statement order).
quizActivities.explanation: Reported statements use statement word order. Present Simple negative 'don't' backshifts to Past Simple negative 'didn't'. Options B, C, D violate backshift or agreement rules.

quizActivities.question: Identify the error in this reported speech sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: She said that she don't like coffee, but she drinks tea everyday.
quizActivities.hint: Check subject-verb agreement AND word choice.
quizActivities.explanation: Two errors: (1) 'She' (third person) needs 'doesn't', not 'don't'. (2) 'Everyday' is an adjective; 'every day' (two words) is the adverbial phrase meaning 'each day'. Both need correction.

quizActivities.question: Choose the best form to complete the sentence:
quizActivities.sentence: He said that if he ____ enough money, he would travel.
quizActivities.hint: This tests the difference between conditional forms in reported speech.
quizActivities.explanation: This is a reported second conditional. Direct: 'If I have enough money, I will travel' → Reported: 'He said that if he had enough money, he would travel.' 'Had' (past simple) is correct after 'if' in reported conditionals.

quizActivities.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct advanced reported speech usage?
options: The researcher stated that the data appears to support the hypothesis, though further analysis is warranted.
The researcher said the data supports the hypothesis.
The researcher stated that the data supported the hypothesis.
The researcher says that the data supports the hypothesis.
quizActivities.correctAnswer: The researcher stated that the data appears to support the hypothesis, though further analysis is warranted.
quizActivities.hint: Look for appropriate register, precise vocabulary, and structural complexity.
quizActivities.explanation: Advanced usage requires not just grammatical correctness but appropriate register and contextual fit. Option A demonstrates hedging ('appears to'), formal vocabulary ('warranted'), and nuanced reporting.

quizActivities.question: Identify the stylistic issue in this formal reported speech:
quizActivities.sentence: The committee said they can't approve the proposal 'cause it's too expensive.
quizActivities.hint: Formal writing avoids contractions and colloquialisms.
quizActivities.explanation: In formal/academic writing, contractions (can't, 'cause, it's) should be expanded (cannot, because, it is). This maintains professional register and clarity.

quizActivities.question: Choose the most precise hedging expression for academic reported speech:
quizActivities.sentence: The study ____ suggest a correlation, though further research is needed.
quizActivities.hint: Academic writing uses hedging to show caution with claims.
quizActivities.explanation: 'Appears to' provides appropriate hedging for academic claims—confident but not absolute. 'Definitely' and 'is proven to' are too strong without conclusive evidence; 'might possibly maybe' is redundant and weakens the argument.

spellingActivities.hint: Subordinating conjunction - shows contrast in reported clauses
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ it was raining, she said she would go out.

spellingActivities.hint: Subordinating conjunction - shows reason in reported explanations
spellingActivities.sentence: He explained that he was late ____ the traffic.

spellingActivities.hint: Transition word - shows contrast between reported statements
spellingActivities.sentence: She said she was tired. ____, she finished her work.

spellingActivities.hint: Transition word - shows result in reported conclusions
spellingActivities.sentence: She studied hard; ____, she passed the exam, he reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Preposition - shows contrast with noun/gerund in reported clauses
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the rain, she said she would go hiking.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal transition - adds supporting information in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: The report stated the plan was efficient. ____, it was cost-effective.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal contrast marker - acknowledges but persists in reported context
spellingActivities.sentence: The odds were against us. ____, we succeeded, she said.

spellingActivities.hint: Formal result marker - shows logical outcome in reported explanations
spellingActivities.sentence: Funding was cut. ____, the project halted, they reported.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced preposition - formal contrast with noun phrase in reported speech
spellingActivities.sentence: ____ the challenges, the team delivered excellent results, he stated.

spellingActivities.hint: Advanced adverb - formal time reference meaning 'until now' in reported context
spellingActivities.sentence: The data, ____ unavailable, now supports the hypothesis, the researcher reported.
